summary: Michael Aris was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied under David Snellgrove at the University of London (PhD 1978) and held posts at the University of Oxford (1978–1999) and Harvard University (~1992–1993).

Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Michael Balk completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall studied at the University of Cambridge and worked in art history. He held posts at the Warburg Institute (1959–1961, 1965, 1981), Courtauld Institute of Art (~1982–1986), and UC Berkeley (1987).

Michael Bernays studied at the universities of Bonn and Heidelberg, including under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor at the University of Washington (~1976), where he is attested as Professor Emeritus of Hindi in 2026.

Michael Carrithers studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford (doctorate ~1978). Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he lectured at Oxford (~1982–1985) and held posts at Durham University from 1982, becoming Professor of Anthropology in 1992.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (~1983–1987), and held a faculty post at the University of Sydney.
Michael J. Conway is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as faculty at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Michael Eido Luetchford worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford (~1964–1967) and studied under the traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima (~1977–2007).

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich by 1984. He worked at the University of Munich (1983–1986) and served as Professor at the University of Hamburg (1994–2021).

Michael Hahn specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (PhD 1967) and held professorships at the University of Bonn (1974) and the University of Marburg (1988–2007).
Michael Harack studied religious studies and Sinology at McMaster University, completing his Master of Arts under James A. Benn (attested 2007).

Michael Hutt studied at SOAS University of London and the University of London (doctorate ~1984). In Indology and linguistics, he held several posts at SOAS from 1987, including Head of the South Asia Department (1995–1999).
Michael I. Como works in religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology, having studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He holds a post at Columbia University (attested 2009, 2026).

Michael J. Walsh works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cape Town and UC Santa Barbara, where he worked under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael Janda works in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD under Heiner Eichner at the University of Vienna (-1996), habilitated at the University of Zurich, and took a chair at the University of Münster in 2002.

Michael Jansen worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at RWTH Aachen University (Promotion 1979), served as Dean of Architecture there (1988–1999), and was founding rector of the German University of Technology in Oman (2007–2008).

Michael Jay Sweet studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completing a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1977). He later served there as clinical assistant professor of psychiatry (attested 1996, 2006).

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD under Mark Juergensmeyer at UC Santa Barbara (~2003–2008) and held professorships at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2013–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (1969–1972) and SOAS University of London (1987–1990).
